# Fact0 Documentation

> Experimental, self-hosted execution inspection and audit records for AI agents, with Python and Claude Code integrations. MIT licensed; best-effort maintenance without an SLA.

## Start here

- [Installation and owner setup](/quickstart)
- [Deterministic Python example](/sdk/python/installation)
- [Claude Code collector](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Verification and signed exports](/guides/verification)
- [Storage, backup and restore](/guides/self-hosting)
- [Security and capture limitations](/guides/security)

Configure every integration with its explicit local destination, normally `http://localhost:8000`. SDK package defaults retained for compatibility are not installation instructions. Never send test traffic to a hosted Fact0 endpoint.

## Interfaces and package identities

- Audit records: `/v1`; execution telemetry: `/api/v1`.
- Python: distribution `fact0-sdk`, import `fact0`. Install the SDK from this release checkout for the supported first-use example.
- TypeScript: `@fact0/sdk`, import `Fact0Client`.
- Go: `github.com/fact0-ai/fact0/sdk/go`.
- Canonical schemas: root `openapi/audit.v1.yaml` and `openapi/telemetry.v1.yaml`, copied into `docs/openapi` by `scripts/sync-openapi.sh`.

## Supported release

One owner and workspace, password login, authenticated inspection, timelines, DAGs, replay, basic usage, chain verification and exports. Raw Claude capture is the default and stores supported prompts, source and tool output in the local instance. Hashes and metadata-only capture are selectable. Prepare the collector binary before starting Claude; hooks never download it.

Billing, invitations, founder administration, Spotlight, email, external alert webhooks, public sharing, policy enforcement and OTLP are disabled. Records do not expire automatically. A valid audit chain establishes integrity of recorded entries, not completeness of real-world activity or protection from an operator replacing the whole database and its keys.
